But there’s a lot to be learned from other people’s mistakes, and sometimes those lessons are far more important than anything we learn from their successes. A shrimp tank water change should improve water quality, not shock the animals living in it. Today, The Veil needed some attention. The sponge filter was filthy, and it took several rinses in old tank water to remove all that accumulated waste. But even with all that buildup, I only changed about 10–15% of the water. Why? Because shrimp can be incredibly sensitive to sudden changes in temperature, pH, GH, and KH. With a growing colony and baby shrimp everywhere, stability is my priority. I used temperature-matched, dechlorinated water and refilled slowly to minimize sudden changes. A small water change isn’t a universal rule, but it’s the approach that makes sense for this tank right now. Clean water matters. Stable water matters just as much. #GlasswaterGuild #ShrimpKeeping #NeocaridinaShrimp #AquariumMaintenance #shrimptank
